note: Labeled from candidates.txt only (grouped-by-keyword excerpt of the corpus), before any retrieval code exists. queries.query: Guest is asking for a student discount
queries.note: New entry, 2026-08-13, added per explicit direction to cover discount/coupon/special-rate requests. Corpus-wide search across all guest messages for discount/coupon/special rate/cheaper/reduced price/best price phrasing (checked both guest and host senders, to rule out the request only surviving in a host-authored quote) found exactly one genuine discount ask in the whole corpus: 1219 (reservation:21cf0871, same thread as the door-code-wrong and listing-photos entries elsewhere in this file -- reusing this thread for a third entry is intentional, same convention as 378d459c and cfcb2b15 elsewhere), 'PLEASE GIVE US A STUDENT DISCOUNT, we are on a very very tight budget.' The request also named a second recalled instance -- a guest traveling from Australia asking for a discount -- but this was checked and does not exist as described: the only Australia-related messages in the corpus (145/inquiry:9bcd0c94 and 284/reservation:f0983e1e, identical text sent to both an inquiry and its linked reservation) read in full as 'Hi Samir, we are visiting Washing DC part of our US trip from Australia :)' with no discount language anywhere in either thread, and the host declined the booking for unrelated availability reasons. Also checked 199 (reservation:e693fe1e, a self-described PhD student) -- mentions being a student but never asks for a discount anywhere in that thread either. Per the explicit 'don't force it' instruction, only the one confirmed instance is included rather than padding the set with these near-misses. Business-practice context (does not affect what belongs in expected, documented for reference only): current practice is not to give refunds, discounts, or coupons -- the guest's ask is the retrieval target regardless of how or whether it was resolved. Human review pass, 2026-08-15: added a second, real instance -- 1458 (inquiry:8330b4bc, Josh, a pre-booking inquiry, not a confirmed reservation): 'I just wanted to ask whether you might have any flexibility on the price for the five-night stay or be able to offer a small discount?' Re-verified both 1219 and 1458 fresh against hospitable.db at time of write. TYPE DECISION: reclassified lexical -> paraphrase. 1219 is near-verbatim ('STUDENT DISCOUNT'); 1458 shares the bare word 'discount' but leads with much softer, indirect phrasing ('flexibility on the price') and never mentions being a student at all -- a genuinely different phrasing of the same underlying ask, not just a quieter version of the same one. 'Lexical' in this file has meant the WHOLE expected set shares near-verbatim wording with the query, not just one member of it; once the set contains a message that only shares a single word and leads with different phrasing, paraphrase is the more accurate label. Same precedent as the stay-extension entry, which was classified paraphrase rather than lexical for an analogous reason (a mixed-directness expected set, not a uniformly literal one). MERGE-VS-SPLIT DECISION: merged into this entry rather than creating a separate inquiry-stage entry. The underlying guest intent (wanting a lower price) is the same regardless of whether the guest has already booked -- booking stage is a data-source distinction (which API entity type the message happens to live in), not a different intent, and this file already mixes inquiry and reservation entities freely within a single entry when the intent is the same (see the early-check-in entry, which includes both inquiry:ab600c9c/inquiry:eb6e254f and multiple reservation entities in one expected set). A retrieval system asked about discount requests should surface pre-booking asks too, not just post-booking ones, so keeping them together is the more useful test, not just the more convenient one.

Human review pass, 2026-08-12: this entry originally ran through the full thread (934...924), which conflated two different guest problems -- (1) the early luggage drop-off negotiation before arrival, and (2) a separate incident 9 days later on actual check-in day, when the guest arrived to find their room locked. queries.query: In reservation 378d459c, the guest arrived to find their room locked -- what happened and how did the host resolve it?
queries.note: New entry, 2026-08-12, split off from q15 (see that entry's note for the full background) -- the second, distinct problem in the same thread: 9 days after the early-luggage-drop-off arrangement was settled, the guest arrives on actual check-in day (2026-05-02) and finds their room locked. Arc: guest arrives, room locked, asks about a key (928) -> host says leave luggage in the living room for now, confirms which room (927) -> guest confirms (926) -> host says they'll notify once it's unlocked (925) -> ~4 hours later, host confirms the room is unlocked, luggage moved inside, key left (924). FLAG for the record: this was requested as covering 'locked out because another guest has the door,' but the actual thread never states why the room was locked -- no mention anywhere of another guest occupying it, a hardware fault, or a cleaning/turnover delay specifically. The one nearby mention of 'other guests will still be in the space' (932) was about the EARLIER, separate early-access-before-2PM window, not this actual-check-in-day incident, so it doesn't obviously explain this one either. Rather than force the 'another guest has the door' framing onto content that doesn't say that, this entry describes what the thread actually shows: a locked room on arrival with an unstated cause, resolved by the host over several hours. Deliberately not folded into the q06/q07/q08 access-failure group (from the same review pass) -- those three are specifically about a non-working/wrong door CODE preventing entry; this is about a room that was locked by the host's side pending some unstated readiness condition, a different failure mode, even though thematically adjacent.

queries.note: New entry, 2026-08-10, angle 2 (topic-scoped, non-adjacent) rather than angle 1 (single bounded arc) -- a different capability than q14/q15: can retrieval group topically-related messages that are NOT adjacent and NOT part of one continuous exchange, scattered across a long, multi-topic thread? reservation:24117b53 is one of the three long threads this pass confirmed is NOT a genuine single-topic multi-turn case (see q15's note) -- several unrelated exchanges (internship chat, cleaning-access questions, neighborhood recs, a dishwasher malfunction, another-guest heads-up) sit between the kitchen-equipment moments used here. Found by a systematic keyword search across guest messages (pot, pan, thermometer, knife, cutting board, blender, toaster, kettle, microwave, stove, oven, fridge, dish, spice, cookware, utensil, plate, bowl, glass, mug) plus a full read of the thread. Three genuinely separate moments, guest-authored only (matching this file's convention for 'what did the guest ask' queries): 1441 (pots and pans, day 3 of the stay) -- 17 days and dozens of unrelated messages later -- 1421 (a baking sheet) and 1418 (aluminum foil, ~1 minute after 1421, same live exchange). Deliberately excluded 1429 ('trouble starting the dishwasher') -- that's a malfunction report about a kitchen appliance, a different intent than asking whether/for an item, even though it touches the same room. This exclusion is a judgment call, not a certainty; a differently-scoped version of this query could reasonably include it.

queries.query: Did a guest ever report a smoke detector or fire alarm going off in the unit?
queries.note: No smoke detector, fire, or safety-alarm content appears anywhere in candidates.txt across any of the topic groups, threads, or the random sample. Genuine true-negative: the honest answer is 'no match in this corpus.' Tests whether retrieval (especially embeddings) forces a confident-but-wrong nearest neighbor instead of correctly returning nothing above threshold. Human review pass, 2026-08-15: tightened query text (was: 'Did a guest ever report a smoke detector going off or a fire safety issue?') to remove the broad 'or a fire safety issue' clause. That phrasing was found, via the embeddings baseline, to pull in messages 311 and 308 (reservation:47dff4ed) -- a guest reporting a strong gas smell, explicitly framed 'por seguridad' (for safety) -- as false-positive top results, since a gas smell genuinely is a safety issue in the general sense even though no smoke detector or fire alarm was involved. Confirmed with the user: no smoke detector or fire alarm ever went off anywhere in this corpus -- the gas smell is a real, separate incident. It does NOT belong in this entry's scope, which is now explicitly limited to smoke-detector/fire-alarm hardware events. The gas-smell report now has its own entry (see 'guest reports smelling gas' paraphrase entry) documenting a distinct, related-but-different safety topic -- same adjacent-but-different-intent pattern as the q08/q09 split elsewhere in this file. This entry remains a genuine true negative under its tightened, hardware-specific scope: re-verified live against hospitable.db, zero smoke-detector/fire-alarm content anywhere in the corpus.

queries.query: Has any guest ever asked if there's a pool at the property?
queries.note: New entry, 2026-08-10. Verified by a live, case-insensitive search across every guest message in hospitable.db for 'pool' and 'swimming' (not just absence from candidates.txt): zero matches, either word, anywhere in the corpus. A DC rowhouse obviously has no pool, but 'is there a pool' is exactly the kind of reflexive question guests ask about almost any short-term rental regardless of property type, so it's a realistic negative, not a contrived one. Same failure mode as q17/q21: does retrieval correctly return nothing, or does it confidently surface an unrelated amenity message as a false positive?
